events.name: 부산정치파동 계엄 결정·승인·지휘선
legal_authority: ROK Constitution martial-law provisions; exact 1952 proclamation text still required
events.finding: Rhee told Van Fleet the Cabinet had decided on martial law, that he approved it, specifically suggested including Pusan, and arranged that the martial-law commander take orders directly from him. This materially narrows command attribution beyond the earlier Embassy inference, while the exact Korean written decree/countersignature chain remains open.

events.name: 소민호 및 야당계 국회의원 체포
events.finding: The arrest campaign is contemporaneously documented, but individual warrants and issuer identities remain unverified. Do not collapse martial-law command attribution into proof that Rhee personally ordered each arrest.

events.name: 직선제 개헌 요구와 국회 해산 최후통첩
events.finding: FRUS footnote based on telegram 1244 records that Rhee told his Cabinet he was asking the Prime Minister to communicate a 24-hour ultimatum: pass direct presidential election or he would dissolve the Assembly.

events.name: 내각회의의 국회의원 집단구금 제안과 대통령 지시
events.finding: Yi Pom-sok suggested arresting all Assemblymen and putting them in a stockade; the Prime Minister rebuked the suggestion. Rhee instead ordered Yi not to block demonstrators coming into Pusan. These are distinct actions and must not be merged into a presidential order to arrest all legislators.

events.name: 발췌개헌 표결 확보와 후속 입법
proposed_by: Rhee government and compromise committee actors
events.finding: Police compelled or escorted absent legislators to the Assembly Hall; on July 4 the compromise amendment substance passed 163-0 with three abstentions among 166 present, followed by implementing legislation July 15. Domestic stenographic record remains a priority cross-check.

events.name: 반공포로 석방 대통령 명령
events.finding: Unlike many contested attribution questions, presidential authorship is direct: Rhee's same-day statement says he ordered the release on his own responsibility and instructed governors and police to care for released prisoners. Lower-level operational orders still require Korean records.

events.name: 포로석방 후 UNC·미국 대응과 지휘권 위기
events.finding: US records treated the release as unilateral presidential action and raised whether a different command arrangement would be required unless Rhee accepted UNC authority.

events.name: 정전 반대·상호방위조약·한국군 증강 협상
events.finding: ROK proposals explicitly tied recognition of the June 18 prisoner release to broader demands including industrialization, defense strength and an automatic US defense commitment. These proposals are bargaining positions, not accepted treaty terms.
